title: Find Confidence, Avoid Ego
coreMove: Trust the preparation enough to act, then keep the ego small enough to listen; stillness needs both readiness and correction in the room at the same time.

exampleSpecs.audience: coaches teaching confidence without hero worship
exampleSpecs.stakes: young players may copy public swagger without learning private standards
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A coach changes the drill standard without using a two-panel scene.

exampleSpecs.audience: young athletes learning the difference between skill and self-command
exampleSpecs.stakes: public mastery may hide private appetite if nobody names the missing practice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A learner's confusion about Tiger Woods becomes the teaching case.

exampleSpecs.audience: public historians writing about power and restraint
exampleSpecs.stakes: an exhibit may make restraint look like passivity instead of command
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: show thought-by-thought correction inside the writer's head

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders tempted to turn preparation into theater
exampleSpecs.stakes: a famous example may feed ego instead of disciplined confidence
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A coach uses Washington's resignation to reframe what deserves attention.

exampleSpecs.audience: team leads presenting under public praise
exampleSpecs.stakes: the lead may either feed ego with certainty or hide readiness from fear
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: force the only binary dilemma in the chapter and then model the middle path

exampleSpecs.audience: officers studying confidence under public power
exampleSpecs.stakes: students may confuse restraint with refusal to lead
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: let two named people find the lesson through exchange
